title: Ch 6 Test: Control and Coordination
subject: Science
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Internal choice is given in some questions.
Section A: 1 mark each. Section B: 2 marks each. Section C: 3 marks each. Section D: 5 marks. Section E: case-based, 4 marks.

questions.q: Which of the following is a plant hormone?
The gap between two neurons is called a:
Which hormone regulates the blood sugar level?
The bending of a plant shoot towards light is called:

**Assertion (A):** Iodised salt is advised in our diet.
**Reason (R):** Iodine is needed by the thyroid gland to make thyroxin.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.answer: (a). A deficiency of iodine can cause goitre.

questions.q: What is a reflex action? Give two examples.
questions.answer: A sudden, automatic response to a stimulus that happens without conscious thinking. Examples (any two): pulling the hand away from a hot object, blinking when a bright light falls on the eyes, sneezing, knee-jerk.

or.q: How do the leaves of the touch-me-not plant respond to touch? How is this movement different from a shoot bending towards light?
or.answer: The leaves fold up and droop when touched. Cells change shape by changing the amount of water in them, and there is no growth involved. The bending of a shoot towards light is a growth-related movement: cells on the shaded side grow longer because of auxin.
marking: Touch-me-not: water/cell shape change, no growth: 1

questions.q: Why is adrenaline called the 'emergency hormone'? Give two of its effects on the body.
questions.answer: It is secreted by the adrenal glands directly into the blood when we are scared or in danger, and it prepares the body to respond. Effects (any two): the heart beats faster, sending more oxygen to the muscles; blood supply to the digestive system and skin is reduced; the breathing rate increases.

questions.q: Answer the following about a neuron:

subparts.q: In which part of a neuron is information first acquired?
Through which part does the information travel as an electrical impulse?
subparts.answer: From the dendrite to the cell body, and then along the axon to its end.

subparts.q: How is the impulse passed on to the next neuron?
subparts.answer: At the end of the axon, the electrical impulse sets off the release of chemicals. These cross the gap (synapse) and start a similar electrical impulse in the dendrite of the next neuron.

For each condition, name the gland and the hormone involved: (a) dwarfism, (b) diabetes, (c) goitre.
subparts.answer: (a) Pituitary gland: deficiency of growth hormone in childhood. (b) Pancreas: insulin not secreted in proper amounts. (c) Thyroid gland: thyroxin, due to iodine deficiency.

subparts.q: Why is a feedback mechanism important in the secretion of hormones? Give an example.
subparts.answer: The timing and amount of hormone released must be precise, and feedback mechanisms regulate this. Example: when blood sugar rises, cells of the pancreas detect it and secrete more insulin. As the sugar level falls, insulin secretion is reduced.

or.q:
(a) Name the three main regions of the brain and give one function of each. [3]
(b) How is the brain protected? [2]
or.answer: (a) Forebrain: the main thinking part, with areas for sensory information, voluntary actions, hunger and so on. Midbrain: controls many involuntary actions. Hindbrain: the cerebellum controls posture and balance, and the medulla controls blood pressure, salivation and vomiting. (b) The brain sits inside a bony box (the skull/cranium) and is surrounded by a fluid-filled balloon that acts as a shock absorber.

sections.title: Section E
sections.note: Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

questions.q: A student placed a potted plant near a window for a week. The shoot bent towards the window, while the roots grew downwards. The student read that a hormone made at the shoot tip diffuses towards the shaded side of the shoot. This makes the cells on that side grow longer, so the shoot bends towards light.

subparts.q: Name the response of the shoot towards light.
Name the hormone involved, and say where it is made.
subparts.answer: Auxin, made at the shoot tip.

subparts.q: Explain why the shoot bends towards light. Name the response of the roots to gravity.
subparts.answer: Auxin diffuses to the shaded side, where the cells grow longer than on the lit side, so the shoot bends towards light. Roots show positive geotropism (they grow downwards).
